title: Small habits, big difference
description: Money habits beat money overhauls — five tiny routines that quietly add up.

body.heading: Habits run on autopilot
paragraphs: Willpower is tiring; habits are cheap. A small routine — checking your balance with breakfast, moving $2 to savings on Fridays — repeats without a daily debate, and repetition is where results come from.
Attach each new habit to something you already do. Habits with a trigger survive; habits that rely on remembering usually fade.

body.heading: Five tiny starters
paragraphs: Try one at a time: a weekly money check-in, a 24-hour pause on wants, rounding purchases up and saving the difference, a no-spend day each week, and reviewing subscriptions every few months.
Pick the one that feels easiest. Success with a small habit builds confidence for the next one far better than a grand plan that collapses.

body.heading: Forgive the misses
paragraphs: Missed a week? Habits bend; they do not break unless you abandon them. Restart at the next trigger, without a guilt tax.

takeaway: Choose one tiny money habit, attach it to an existing routine, and let repetition do the work.
